audits.title: Full Platform Review — Pre-Alpha
audits.scope: Full platform: public site, architecture, chat app design, provider data pipeline design, roadmap, privacy policy, terms of use, live chat testing, Brain design spec (GPT Reader v6.1)
audits.overall_assessment: Architecturally sound, engineering quality exceeds expectations for pre-alpha. Primary risks are strategic and legal, not technical. Three highest-priority items: (1) tool registry to close globals() security gap, (2) legal counsel on FDA/clinical decision support boundary, (3) lock architecture docs behind NDA before Alpha.

audits.title: BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 prompt_log Design Audit
audits.scope: Design and requirements only — BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 prompt_log feature. No code or runtime artifacts.
audits.overall_assessment: Plausible and generally sound design. Moderate clarity and governance gaps to address in Phase 2 GPT review.

records.title: BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 prompt_log Design Audit
records.scope: Design and requirements only — BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 prompt_log feature under OPS-AGENT-COMMS. No code, infrastructure, or runtime artifacts reviewed.
records.overall_assessment: Plausible and generally sound design. Append-only model, actor attribution, and dual timestamps match standard audit-log patterns. Moderate clarity and governance gaps around time semantics, immutability controls, truncation policy, credential-handling responsibility, and operational visibility into grooming behavior. Gaps should be addressed in next design iteration before implementation.
records.executive_summary: The prompt_log requirements form a plausible and generally sound design for solving ephemeral Claude sessions and missing short-term conversation audit trails. The specification contains moderate clarity and governance gaps that do not render the design unworkable but should be addressed before implementation begins.

findings_detail.title: Problem statement is strong and well scoped
findings_detail.detail: The problem statement clearly articulates the current defect: Claude sessions are ephemeral, conversation history is not persisted, and there is no audit trail or substrate for downstream grooming, summarization, or automation. The proposed solution is directly responsive and matches common audit-log patterns.

findings_detail.title: Efficacy depends on 24-hour horizon being sufficient
findings_detail.detail: For compliance, incident reconstruction, or longitudinal model-behavior analysis, 24 hours is short by typical audit-log norms. For ChatHealthy's current stage, this is an accepted risk.
findings_detail.recommendation: Document that prompt_log is a short-term operational log, not a regulatory audit log. Plan a follow-on story for long-horizon archival.

findings_detail.title: Roles vs. actors are well distinguished but not fully formalized
findings_detail.detail: The spec lists actor and role fields but does not define allowed values, casing rules, or a registry process. Inconsistent actor/role strings reduce usefulness for analytics.
findings_detail.recommendation: Add a requirement that actor values must be drawn from a documented registry or canonical naming convention.

findings_detail.title: Time semantics and authority are under-specified
findings_detail.detail: The spec does not state which timestamp field is used for grooming, how daylight savings time is handled, or whether 'older than 24 hours' is inclusive or exclusive at the boundary.
findings_detail.recommendation: Amend TR12-TR15 to state explicitly that grooming is based on timestamp_utc, with a precise rule ('delete utterances where timestamp_utc < now_utc - 24h'), and treat timestamp_pst as convenience rendering only.

findings_detail.title: Append-only guarantees are conceptually strong but not tied to specific controls
findings_detail.detail: TR8 and TR14 specify append-only, but requirements do not describe any control that enforces immutability at the store level nor how drift would be detected.
findings_detail.recommendation: Add a technical requirement stating the underlying collection must either be technically append-only or support a separate corrections record while preserving originals.

findings_detail.title: Binary-exclusion rule is clear but silently dropping content is a risk
findings_detail.detail: Silent discarding creates a risk that interactions referencing attachments are partially represented with no indication that key context was missing.
findings_detail.recommendation: Refine TR9/TR11 to allow a short marker such as '[binary content omitted]' alongside textual content.

findings_detail.title: Credential-handling requirement is inconsistent between TR10 and clarified scope
findings_detail.detail: TR10 states credentials are redacted, but Boss clarified security is handled in a separate epic. Leaving TR10 in the spec while treating credential handling as out-of-scope will confuse future reviewers.
findings_detail.recommendation: Either remove TR10 and reference the security epic, or keep TR10 with a cross-reference that credential redaction is enforced via shared middleware owned by the security epic.

findings_detail.title: Tool-result truncation policy is under-specified
findings_detail.detail: TR11 does not state whether the first 500 characters are kept, whether summaries can replace full content, or whether both retained prefix and length of omission must be logged.
findings_detail.recommendation: Clarify TR11: (a) truncation is strictly by prefix, (b) summaries are not permitted, (c) logged message must include standard marker.

findings_detail.title: System-reminder exclusion rule conflicts slightly with 'no visible chars excluded' principle
findings_detail.detail: The spec does not clearly distinguish between internal non-visible system reminders and user-visible system messages.
findings_detail.recommendation: Refine TR16 to specify that only system-reminder content not rendered to any actor UI is excluded.

findings_detail.title: Collection-level metadata is thin
findings_detail.detail: TR17 and TR18 are vague about where and how metadata lives. Without stricter documentation, future contributors may fail to keep schema and operational behavior synchronized.
findings_detail.recommendation: Expand TR17/TR18 to require specific path/location for schema.json, explicit mapping between retention and Azure Function schedule, and a short prompt log protocol document.

findings_detail.title: Current brain implementation (Mongo + JSON + scripts) is a known but material architecture risk
findings_detail.detail: The hybrid 'one collection plus files' arrangement is common in very early-stage projects but does not represent a clean data architecture for a scaling product.
findings_detail.recommendation: Record as known architecture debt. Plan a separate 'Brain Data Architecture' initiative once BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 is stable.

findings_detail.title: No explicit logging of grooming failures or gaps
findings_detail.detail: There is no explicit requirement that grooming failures or communication gaps be logged. Without a trace, it is difficult to distinguish 'no conversations in last 24 hours' from 'grooming silently misbehaved.'
findings_detail.recommendation: Add a requirement that the grooming Azure Function write a minimal operational summary to prompt_log (as an OpsAgent actor) or a sibling collection, including counts of deleted utterances and any errors encountered.

clarification_record.q: Should the audit consider only internal consistency, or also efficacy and architectural fit?
clarification_record.a: Both. The audit must consider whether the plan effectively addresses the stated problem.

clarification_record.q: Is the current brain implementation (Mongo + JSON + scripts) in scope?
clarification_record.a: Known gap and accepted risk for an 8-day-old enterprise; cite but do not treat as blocking flaw.

clarification_record.q: Which timestamp is authoritative and who owns the 24-hour window?
clarification_record.a: Timestamp in the record is authoritative. Azure Function App owns 24-hour retention behavior.

clarification_record.q: Should lost utterances be treated as a hard failure?
clarification_record.a: Utterances should not be lost in principle, but detecting gaps is hard; accepted risk.
No. Boss talks to Claude and GPT sequentially; concurrency is an implementation detail.
Binary objects may be silently dropped; no hard error required.

clarification_record.q: Is credential redaction in scope for this feature?
clarification_record.a: No. Security is handled in a separate epic.

clarification_record.q: For long tool results, how strict is the 500-character rule?
clarification_record.a: Use judgment. Business prefers no redaction, but truncation acceptable where necessary.

clarification_record.q: How are actor and role defined?
clarification_record.a: Actors are humans or components; roles are functional stances.

clarification_record.q: How should mixed system-reminder and user content be handled?
clarification_record.a: Anything visible to the actor after control is handed over should not be excluded.

clarification_record.q: How does schema.json relate to grooming?
clarification_record.a: Schema JSON defines collections; grooming is owned by the Azure Function.

records.description: Perplexity design audit of BIZOPS-CHATLOG-001 prompt_log: 12 findings, 0 critical, 4 moderate gaps, 5 minor gaps, 1 strength. Design validated with gaps to address in Phase 2.

records.title: External Audit — ChatHealthy.ai Platform Review
records.scope: Full platform review: public site, architecture, chat app design, provider data pipeline design, roadmap, privacy policy, terms of use, live chat testing, Brain design spec (GPT Read-Only Query Service v6.1)
records.executive_summary: ChatHealthy.ai demonstrates unusually coherent architecture and production-grade data engineering for a pre-alpha solo founder project. The three-app separation (Cloudflare static / HuggingFace chat / Azure pipelines) is clean and independently scalable. The Brain governance system (Claude engineer + GPT architect + Boss tiebreaker) is a novel and effective SDLC for an AI-native company with no human developers. The primary risks are strategic (IP exposure, state coverage, regulatory positioning) rather than architectural. The platform is ready to proceed to Alpha with the caveats documented below.

findings.title: Three-application separation is clean and well-reasoned
findings.detail: App 1 (Cloudflare static), App 2 (HuggingFace chat — React + FastAPI), App 3 (Azure Durable Functions pipelines) each scale and deploy independently. No business logic leaks between layers. The static site costs nothing at rest.

findings.title: Production-grade pipeline engineering
findings.detail: 8.9M NPI records in 35 minutes with 32 workers. Idempotent upserts on (load_id, record_id), byte-aligned partitions, multi-pass county enrichment with provenance tagging, Template Method worker hierarchy, discrepancy reporter.

findings.title: Safety system is well-designed for a health application
findings.detail: Dual-trigger OR logic (keyword + Haiku semantic classifier) with fail-safe default. IP-based lockout with DB persistence and audit trail preservation on unlock.
findings.recommendation: Get legal review of whether the emergency detection system could classify you as a clinical decision support tool under FDA guidance. Estimated cost: $5K consultation.

findings.title: Pipeline framework is correctly designed for AI-operated company
findings.detail: The bespoke Durable Functions orchestrator with PipelineWorkerBase Template Method pattern is the right choice for a company where Claude is the developer.

findings.title: globals().get(name) tool dispatch is a security surface
findings.detail: Chat app _handle_tool_calls() looks up functions by name in globals(). If Claude hallucinates a tool name that matches any global function, it executes.
findings.recommendation: Implement a simple allowlist registry: TOOL_REGISTRY = {'find_providers': find_providers, ...}. One-hour fix.

findings.title: Durable Functions status URL exposes orchestration state without authentication
findings.detail: The 202 Accepted response includes a statusQueryGetUri with an Azure-generated webhook code. Anyone with that URL can poll load_id, record counts, and worker details without authentication.
findings.recommendation: Proxy the status check through /api/Router (authenticated), strip statusQueryGetUri from the 202 response.

findings.title: main.py monolith (1,323 lines) is a velocity blocker
findings.detail: Router logic, safety system, provider search, tool definitions, context loading, consent flow, and error handling all in one file.
findings.recommendation: Correctly prioritized for current sprint. The FindCare/EvaluateCare component separation requires this decomposition.

findings.title: Three-state coverage is thin but rationale is sound
findings.detail: Delaware, Mississippi, and Virginia cover less than 2% of US population. Pipeline architecture can handle all states.
findings.recommendation: All states should be live by Alpha (April 30).

findings.title: Emergency keyword list has coverage gaps
findings.detail: Missing: burns, drowning, trauma (car accident, gunshot, stabbing), diabetic emergency, childbirth.

findings.title: Vector search hard cap of 10 results is too restrictive
findings.detail: Provider search caps at safe_limit = min(int(limit), 10). County-level searches in common specialties will hit this immediately.

findings.title: FIPS hack (ASN-4AFBDA) should be resolved in next pipeline run
findings.detail: 2,579 providers have county.fips set but county.name blank. Root cause fix committed but not re-run.

findings.title: DeepSeek disclosure in privacy policy is incomplete
findings.detail: Privacy policy discloses DeepSeek AI is headquartered in PRC but does not specify what data flows to DeepSeek.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether user conversation data is ever processed by DeepSeek.

findings.title: Architecture documentation is publicly accessible and constitutes a detailed blueprint
findings.detail: Architecture, chat app design, and pipeline design docs are published on the public site. Detailed enough to save a competitor months.
findings.recommendation: Lock architecture docs behind access gate before Alpha. Keep chat demo public.

findings.title: Documentation inconsistencies
findings.detail: Copyright year mismatch, VA listed in chat but not design doc, broken anchor link, non-functional nav button.

findings.title: Brain governance system is an effective SDLC for AI-native company
findings.detail: The Claude-GPT-Boss triangle functions as a complete development organization. The adversarial review process on the GPT Reader design spec produced a disciplined, zero-open-disputes result.

findings.title: Brain lock has no deadlock recovery
findings.detail: R32 Brain lock prevents concurrent modification but has no TTL, no deadlock recovery if Claude crashes mid-write.
findings.recommendation: Add TTL (10 minutes) and Boss-override release. Address before GPT Reader production.

findings.title: Server-side scope enforcement must be independent of Claude
findings.detail: GPT Reader security relies on Claude faithfully proxying calls. Azure Function must independently validate every request against allowlist.

findings.title: Audit should cover Claude's actions too
findings.detail: R26 audits GPT reads but Claude — the most privileged actor — has no audit trail for sync operations and manifest modifications.

records.overall_assessment: The platform is architecturally sound and the engineering quality exceeds expectations for pre-alpha. The primary risks are strategic and legal, not technical. The three highest-priority action items are: (1) implement the tool registry to close the globals() security gap (current sprint, 1 hour), (2) get legal counsel on FDA/clinical decision support boundary (before Alpha), and (3) lock architecture docs behind NDA access before Alpha. The Brain governance system and the AI-native operating model are genuine innovations that should be preserved and strengthened.
records.description: Perplexity full platform review: 18 findings, 0 critical, 3 high, 9 medium. Architecture validated.
